newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares in smart rally on Bajaj Auto bonus.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares in smart rally on Bajaj Auto bonus.

text.p: Shares rallied smartly to close higher at Bombay exchanges on Wednesday, buoyed by hopes of a bonus share issue by scootermaker Bajaj Auto, traders said.
"This has completely changed the market sentiment," said Neeraj Roy, head of institutional sales at Prime Broking.
Bajaj Auto said its board would meet on May 19 to consider a bonus equity issue. The firm's shares ended 68.75 rupees, or eight percent, higher at 918.50, off 934.50--the intra-day high.
Rahul Bajaj, chairman of Bajaj Auto, told reporters after the board meeting that he was not in favour of the firm issuing bonus shares in the ratio of one share for every one share held.
"The market revival has come on the back of the Bajaj Auto bonus news," said Rakesh Chandak, an equity dealer at Lloyds Securities, a local firm.
Traders said the bonus announcement took the market by surprise, but said the stock could see some selling pressure after Bajaj said he did not favour a one-for-one bonus issue.
"This is a sentiment-driven market. I would term the market rally as a technical correction that was expected," said the head of dealing at a foreign brokerage.

Activity was focused on select mid-cap stocks which saw buying interest by foreign funds. Among front-benchers, shares of Tata Engineering & Locomotive Company (TELCO), India's largest truck-maker, rose 10.75 rupess to 380.0 in volumes of over 1.02 million shares.
Strong foreign fund bidding helped the stock close higher, market sources said. TELCO's vehicle sales are expected to climb 12 percent during 1996/97 (April-March), they added.
TELCO is expected to release its fiscal 1996/97 results in May. No date has yet been set.
